s: Which period is called Golden Age?
The Horse-Shoe arch was first introduced in the -
x: The Horse-Shoe arch was first introduced in the Alai Darwaza. It was built by Alauddin Khalji.

s: The first true arch in the Sultanate memorial could be seen in
x: Tomb of Balban is located in Mehrauli, New Delhi. It was here that first true arches made their appearance in India.

s: India’s first tomb constructed in the Indo-Islamic style was
x: The notes give Sultan Ghari (1231), built by Iltutmish, as the first Indo-Islamic tomb. Balban's tomb is only the first true arch, so the keyed answer conflicts with the notes and no line supports it.

s: Which sultan built Alai Darwaza?
x: Alai Darwaza (1311) was built by Alauddin Khalji, as is also shown by its association with his other Delhi works.

s: Which among the following is ‘Octagonal tomb’?
x: Octagonal tombs are a Sayyid and Lodi feature, with Sikandar Lodi's tomb as an example. Balban's and Ghiyasuddin's tombs are not octagonal.

s:
Match the following.
List I (Architectural Style)
List II (Associated Dynasty)

A. 'Lotus bud' fringe on the underside of the arch
1. Sharquis

B. Emergence of octagonal tomb
2. Vijayanagara

C. Use of Bodegoi in the pillar
3. Khiljis

D. Massive entrance gate with inclined walls
4. Tughluqs
Codes A B C D
x: The lotus-bud fringe belongs to the Khalji style (A-3). The first octagonal tomb dates to Firoz Tughlaq's reign (B-4), and massive sloping-wall Tughlaq style fits D. This gives 3 4 2 1.

s: Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque in Delhi was built by:
x: The Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque in Delhi was constructed by Qutb-ud-din Aibak, the founder of the Delhi Sultanate. It was built using materials from demolished temples and stands near the Qutub Minar complex, representing the earliest example of Indo- Islamic architecture in India.

s: What is ‘Adhai Din ka Zhonpda’?
x: 5. Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque and Arhai Din Ka Jhonpra are situated respectively at : (a) Delhi and Ajmer (b) Delhi and Lahore (c) Ajmer and Delhi (d) Lahore and Ajmer Jharkhand P.C.S. (Pre) 2021 Ans. (a) 6. Who among the following did not contribute to building the famous ‘Qutb-Minar’? (a) Qutbuddin Aybak (b) Iltutmish (c) Ghiyasuddin Tughluq (d) Firuz Shah Tughluq U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2013 Ans. (c) Qutbuddin Aybak, the founder of the Delhi Sultanate, started construction of the Qutub Minar, which was completed by Iltutmish. The topmost storey was damaged by lightning, which was rebuilt by Firuz Shah Tughluq. Firuz Shah Tughluq rebuilt the fourth floor of Qutub Minar and built the fifth floor. Ghiyasuddin Tughluq contributed nothing to its construction. From the above options, option (c) is the correct answer. 7. The Qutub Minar was completed by : (a) Iltutmish (b) Qutb-ud-din Aibak (c) Ulugh Khan (d) Raziya Sultana (e) None of the above/More than one of the above 67th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2022 Ans. (a)

s: Hauz-e-Sultani is a…
x: Hauz-e-Sultani (Hauz-i-Shamsi) was a reservoir (tank) built by Iltutmish. 'Hauz' means water tank, so the answer is reservoir.

s:
Match the following.
List I (Monuments)
List II (Builder)

A. Quwwat-ul-Islam
1. Alauddin Khilji

B. Hauz Khas in Delhi
2. Iltutmish

C. Adilabad Fort
3. Muhammad bin Tughluq

D. Jama Masjid in Budaun
4. Qutbuddin Aibak
Codes A B C D
x: Quwwat-ul-Islam was built by Aibak (A-4). Hauz Khas has Firoz Tughlaq's madrasa and tomb added on Alauddin's tank, which is why the key pairs it with Alauddin (B-1). The key then gives Adilabad Fort to Muhammad bin Tughluq (C-3) and the Budaun Jama Masjid to Iltutmish (D-2).

s: The Qutab Minar was named after: merican
x: Khwaja Qutb-ud-din There is historical debate about who the Qutab Minar was named after. It is commonly believed to be named in honour of the Sufi saint Khwaja Qutb-ud-din Bakhtiyar Kaki. Construction was started by Qutb-uddin Aibak and completed by Iltutmish.

s: Who amongst the following sultans built the fifth storey of Qutub Minar?
x: Firoz Shah Tughlaq replaced the lightning-damaged top storey with two storeys, making five. Aibak built only the first storey and Iltutmish the 2nd-4th.

s: Who among the following sultans built the fifth storey of Qutub Minar?
x: Firoz Shah Tughlaq replaced the lightning-damaged top storey with two storeys, making five. Aibak built only the first storey and Iltutmish the 2nd-4th.

s: Which one of the following monuments has a dome which is said to be one of the largest in the world?
x: The Gol Gumbaz in Bijapur (Vijayapura), Karnataka, is the 17 th-century mausoleum of Sultan Mohammad Adil Shah, renowned for its massive, unsupported dome—the second-largest in the world after St. Peter's Basilica.

s: Which of the following rulers got the Jantar Mahal of Mandu constructed?
x: Gujari Mahal was constructed by Raja Man Singh Tomar between 1486-1516 A.D. It is a unique piece of architecture.

s: What is the name of the 16th century stepwell that the Archaeological Survey of India recently conserved in collaboration with the World Monuments Fund India?
o: More than one of the above
x: Rajon ki Baoli, located in the Mehrauli Archaeological Park in Delhi, is a four-tiered stepwell built around 1506 by Daulat Khan Lodi, during the reign of Sikandar Lodi. It is an excellent example of Lodi-period architecture and traditional water-engineering techniques. The Archaeological Survey of India (ASI), in collaboration with World Monuments Fund India (WMFI) and the TCS Foundation, has successfully completed the conservation and rejuvenation work of Rajon ki Baoli. 2. A key focus of Viksit Bharat Yatra is to disseminate information and facilitate access to which of the following areas ? (a) Environmental conservation efforts (b) Space exploration advancements (c) Welfare and development schemes (d) Promotion of traditional arts and crafts Uttarakhand P.C.S. (Pre) 2025 Ans. (c) One of the major objectives of the Viksit Bharat Sankalp Yatra is to disseminate information about government welfare and development schemes among citizens and to ensure easy access to these schemes and their benefits. The yatra was flagged off by PM Narendra Modi on November 15, 2023 from Khunti, Jharkhand. This Yatra focuses on raising awareness about government schemes in both rural and urban areas and on expanding the reach of these schemes to eligible beneficiaries.

s: Who of the following has given a detailed description of the postal system found during the Sultanate period?
x: The detailed description of the postal system is obtained from the chronicle journey of Ibn Battuta. He was the resident of Tanzir region of Morocco and came to India during the period of Muhammad Tughluq. ‘Kitab-ul-Rihla’ is his famous book.

s: Medieval traveller and writer Ibn Batuta belonged to which country?
x: Ibn Battuta was born at Tangiers in Morocco (1304), so Morocco is correct; Persia and Afghanistan are not his origin.

s: Which scholar came to India with Mahmud Ghazni –
x: Al-Biruni, a scholar from Khwarizm, came to India with Mahmud of Ghazni and wrote Kitab-ul-Hind. Ibn Battuta, Khusrau and Ferishta belong to other periods.

s:
What is the sequence of arrival of these travellers?
1. Ibn Battuta
2. Tavernier
3. Al-Biruni
4. Manucci
x: (i) Al-Biruni : Al-Biruni was a resident of Khiva (ancient Khwarizm). He was in the court of the last emperor of Khiva dynasty as a scholar and diplomat before Mahmud Ghazni’s victory over India. He came to India with Mahmud Ghazni during his invasion of India. (ii) Ibn Battuta (1333-1342 A.D. ) : He was Moroccan traveller. He came to India during the Sultanate period in the regime of Muhammad-Bin-Tughluq (1325-1351A.D.). Muhammad Tughluq appointed him as ‘Qazi’ of Delhi. Later, he sent him to China as an ambassador in 1342. He composed his travelling experiences in his book “Rihla.” (iii) Jean-Baptiste Tavernier (17th century A.D.) : A French gem merchant and traveller began his voyage the period of Shahjahan. He made six voyages to the East. He wrote his travel accounts in his book "The Six Voyages of John Baptista Tavernier". (iv) Niccolao Manucci (1653-1708 A.D.) : He was an Italian traveller. He reached India from his hometown Venice while travelling to Turkiye and Asia. He had given his services to Prince Dara Shukoh as a cannoneer. Later, he opted for the medical profession. Manucci is famous for his work. "Storia do Mogor or Mogul India, 1653-1708". 7. Who were called ‘Dastar-Bandan’? (a) SufiSaint (b) Khan (c) Malik (d) Ulema U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2014 Ans. (d) During the Sultanate period, high-positioned or designated religious and judicial authorities honourable (Ulema) were collectively known as Dastar-Bandan, because they dressed with an official turban. 8. s:
Match the following authors with their works:
List I
List II
a. Al-Biruni
I. Tariqh-i-Firoz Shahi
b. Minhaj-us-Siraj
II. Tahqiq-i-Hind
c. Ziauddin Barani
III. The Rihla
d. Ibn Battuta
IV. Tabaqat-i-Nasiri
x: Al-Biruni wrote Tahqiq-i-Hind, Minhaj-us-Siraj wrote Tabaqat-i-Nasiri, Barani wrote Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi and Ibn Battuta wrote the Rihla. This gives a-II, b-IV, c-I, d-III.

s: 'Tarikh-i-Firuz Shahi' was written by
x: Tarikh-i- Firuz Shahi is historical account of the reign of Sultan Firuz Shah Tughlaq. Shams Siraj Afif has written this account. Ziauddin Barani has also written history of Tughlaq dynasty under the same name as Tarikh-i-Firuz Shahi.

s: Who is the author of "Tarikh-i-Firujshahi"?
x: The correctly matched list is as follows : Tarikh-i-Hind Al-Biruni Tarikh-i-Delhi Khusrau Rihla Ibn Battuta Tabqat-i-Nasiri Minhaj-us-Siraj (Minhaj-i-Siraj)

s: Which one of the following travelogues has given an insight on the reign of Muhammad bin Tughluq?
o: Francois Bernier’s Travels in the Mogul Empire
x: Ibn Battuta's Rihla was written during his stay in India (1333-1342) under Muhammad bin Tughlaq, so it throws light on that reign. Bernier, Manucci and Tavernier were Mughal-era travellers.

s:
Consider the following text and arrange them in chronological order.

I. Fatwa-I – Jahandari

II. Prithviraj – Raso

III. Kitab-ul-hind

IV. Tabaqat-i-Nasiri
Select the correct answer from the codes given below.
x: The chronological order is Kitab-ul-Hind (c. 1030), Prithviraj Raso (late 12th c.), Tabaqat-i-Nasiri (c. 1260), then Fatawa-i-Jahandari (14th c.), which gives III, II, IV, I.

s:
Consider the following text and arrange them in chronological order:
1. Fatawa-i-Jahandari
2. Prithviraja-Raso
3. Kitab-ul-Hind
4. Tabaqat-i-Nasiri
Select the correct answer from the codes given below.
Codes:
x: Fatawa-i-Jahandari was written by Ziauddin Barani. Prithviraja-Raso is written by Chandarbardai, Kitab-ul-hind is written by Al-Biruni & Tabaqat-i-Nasiri by Minhaz-i-siraj. Hence correct option is option (d).

s: The first writer to use Urdu as the medium of poetic expression was:
x: Amir Khusrau is regarded as one of the earliest poets to use the emerging Hindavi (early Urdu) for poetic and devotional expression. He composed Sufi poetry in both Persian and Hindavi and introduced musical forms such as qaul in qawwali, which incorporated this mixed vernacular language.

s: Who among the following wrote the book 'Khazainul-Futuh'?
x: Khazain-ul-Futuh, on Alauddin Khalji's conquests, was written by Amir Khusrau. Hasan Nizami wrote Taj-ul-Maasir and Minhaj wrote Tabaqat-i-Nasiri.

s: The first writer to use Urdu as the medium of poetic expression was:
x: The first writer to use Urdu as the medium of poetic expression was Amir Khusrau. He compiled several verses in Urdu. He is also known as the originator of Qawwali.

s: The savant of both languages “Hindi and Persian” was –
x: Khusrau was a scholar of both the Hindi (Hindavi) and the Persian languages.

s: Father of new Persian poetry style “Sabak-i-Hindi or Hindustani style was :
x: Amir Khusrau is considered as the father of the new Persian poetry style “Sabak-i-Hindi” or Hindustani style. He called himself ‘Tuti-i-Hind; He used to say that “Na Lafze Hindiwast aj Farsi Kam” which means the words of Hindi are not less than those of the Persian.

s: Who among the following was the first Persian poet to depict Indian environment in his poetry?
x: Amir Khusrau was a prolific classical poet associated with the Royal courts of more than seven rulers of Delhi Sultanate. He was the first Persian poet to depict Indian environment in his poetry.

s: Amir Khusrau, the “Parrot of India,” was born at-
x: 5. Who among the following called himself the ‘Parrot of India’ ? (a) Qutban (b) Usman (c) Amir Khusrau (d) Amir Hasan U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2013 Ans. (c) 6. Amir Khusrau played a pioneering role in the development of – (a) Braj Bhasha (b) Awadhi (c) Khari Boli (d) Bhojpuri U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2008 U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2002 Ans. (c) Amir Khusrau learned various Indian dialects, especially Hindavi, which he loved most. He referred to himself as a 'Turkish-Indian'. He played a pioneering role in the development of Khari Boli.

s: Who among the following is called the ‘Sadi of India’?
x: Amir Hasan-i-Dehlavi is called the ‘Sadi of India’ (Sadi-i- Hind) for his great Ghazals.

s: Which of the following is not associated with the Bhakti Movement?
x: The full name of Amir Khusrau was Abul Hasan Yaminuddin Khusrau. He was a great poet and scholar of his time. He was not related to the Bhakti Movement. Qiran-us-Sadain, Miftah-ul-Futuh, Nuh Sipihr, Ashiqa, Tughluq Nama and Khazain-ul-Futuh are some of the main texts composed by him. Chaitanya Mahaprabhu founded Madhyagauriya sect. Guru Nanak was born in a Khatri family in Punjab (Pakistan). He imagined the shapeless form of God. Vallabhacharya was the second saint of Krishnamargi branch.

s: Who among the following is known as the ‘Father of Hindi Khari Boli?
x: Amir Khusrau is known as the father of Hindi Khari Boli. He was a promoter of new poetic style ‘Sabak-i-Hindi’ or ‘Hindustani Style.’

s: Amir Khusrau played a pioneer role in the development of
x: Amir Khusrau is called the Father of Khari Boli, as his Hindavi verses and riddles led to Rekhta/Urdu. So Khari Boli is correct.

s: Amir Khusrau was court poet of
x: Khusrau served several Sultans and is linked with Alauddin's court, which gave him the title Tuti-i-Hind. Alauddin is the best match among the options; Ibrahim Lodi is outside his period.

s: Who among the following called himself the ‘parrot of India’?
x: Tuti-i-Hind (Parrot of India) was the title of Amir Khusrau. Sadi-i-Hind is Amir Hasan's title, so Amir Hasan is the tempting wrong option.

s: Who among the following was the author of Tarikh-i-Alai, which contains the details of the first few years of Sultan Alauddin Khilji?
x: Khusrau's Khazain-ul-Futuh (Khazain-ul-Futuh-i-Alai) describes Alauddin's conquests, so he is the contemporary author. Barani and Afif wrote Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi.

s: Amir Khusrau was a –
x: Amir Khusrau was a poet, historian, and musician. He was nicknamed as “Tuti-i-Hind.” He was a promoter of Khari Boli of Hindi.

s: “Every pearl in the Royal crown is the crystallised drops of blood fallen from the tearful eyes of the poor peasants” … Who made this statement?
x: The statement is attributed to Amir Khusrau, who criticised the burden on the peasants. The notes do not state this fact.

s: Amir Khusrau was born in
x: Khusrau was born at Patiyali, which lies in the Etah district, so Etah is correct.

s:
Which of the following texts are written by Amir Khusrau ?
1. Khazain-ul-Futuh
2. Nuh Siphir
3. Miftah-ul-Futuh
4. Qiraan-us-Sadain
x: Amir Khusrau composed the following works: • Khaza'in-ul-Futuh • Nuh Sipihr • Miftah-ul-Futuh • Qiran-us-Sa'dain

s:
Consider the following statement about Ziauddin Barani.

I. He was born in Golconda.

II. He was contemporary of Muhammad bin Tughluq.

III. He wrote Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Barani was a companion of Muhammad bin Tughlaq and wrote Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi, so II and III are correct. The notes do not say he was born in Golconda, so statement I is not supported.

s: Who among the following witnessed the reign of Seven Sultans of Delhi?
x: Amir Khusrau served at the courts of seven successive Delhi Sultans; he was a disciple of Nizamuddin Auliya.

s: Which one of the following Sultans of Delhi was refused an audience by Nizamuddin Auliya?
x: Shaikh Nizamuddin Auliya saw the regime of more than seven Sultans, but he never visited their court. Sultan Jalaluddin tried to meet Nizamuddin Auliya through Amir Khusrau but when Nizamuddin Auliya heard that the Sultan was about to come, he moved to Ajodhan. When Alauddin asked him to meet, then Shaikh replied: “There are two doors in my home, if the Sultan comes from one door, I will go out by another.” He was also known as ‘Mehboob-i-Ilahi.’

s: Which of the following musical instruments is not of Indo-Islamic origin?
x: Turkic people brought several instruments like Rabab and Sarangi and a new methodology of music and musical instruments with them. The present Sitar was invented by Khusrau. The credit for inventing Tabla goes to Amir Khusrau. M.P.P.S.C. has marked option (d) as the correct answer which is wrong.

s: ‘Tabla’ was introduced by :
x: Amir Khusrau’s real name was Abul Hasan Yaminuddin Khusrau. He was a great scholar and poet of his time. He was the first author who used Hindi (Hindavi) phrases and words. The musical instruments like Tabla and Sitar were invented by Amir Khusrau in the 13th/14th century.

s: Musical instrument sitar is the combination of:
x: A musical instrument called Sitar was invented by Amir Khusrau. It combined the features of the old Indian Veena and the Iranian Tambura.

s: Which among the following musical instruments is the finest example of Hindu-Muslim harmony in musical instruments?
x: Indian music motivated Muslim society to be passionate about music. Consequently, Amir Khusrau emerged as a great musician during Sultanate period. He invented ‘Sitar’ with a combination of Irani Tamboora and Indian Veena. He combined some Indian and Persian melodies elegantly and introduced some new melody styles like Iman, Zilf, Sajgari, etc.

s: Who among the following had translated Chintamani Bhatt’s Sanskrit text ‘Suka Saptati’ into Persian and gave it the title ‘Tutinama’?
x: Khwaza Ziya-uddin Nakhshabi translated Chintamani Bhatt’s text ‘Suka Saptati’ into Persian and gave it title 'Tutinama'. Nakhshabi was a 14th-century Persian Physician and Sufisaint who migrated to Badayun (UP).

s: The term ‘Apabhramsa’ was used in medieval Sanskrit text to denote
o: early forms of some of the modern Indian language.
x: Apabhramsa denotes the early forms of the modern Indian languages, which grew out of Prakrit. The notes do not cover this.

s: Which was the official language in the Delhi Sultanate?
x: Persian was the elite language of administration in the Sultanate. Urdu grew in camps and bazaars and was not the official language.

s: Who among the following established independent Muslim rule in Malwa?
x: Dilawar Khan Ghuri broke away from Delhi in 1401 and founded independent Malwa; Hoshang Shah only moved the capital to Mandu.

s: Who shifted the capital of the Bahmani Kingdom from Gulbarga to Bidar?
x:
Ahmad Shah I Wali (1422–1436 CE) shifted the Bahmani capital from Gulbarga to Bidar in 1425 CE. Bidar soon developed into a major centre of:
• Persian culture
• Architecture
• Literature
• Islamic learning The city remained the capital of the Bahmani Kingdom until its decline. Hence, the correct answer is Option (1).
Exam Note:
• Capital shifted → Gulbarga → Bidar
• By → Ahmad Shah I

s: Who founded the Bahmani Empire?
x:
The Bahmani Sultanate was founded in 1347 CE by Ala-ud-Din Bahman Shah, better known as Hasan Gangu. He revolted against the Delhi Sultanate under Muhammad bin Tughlaq and established an independent kingdom with Gulbarga as its first capital. The Bahmani Sultanate became the first independent Muslim kingdom in the Deccan and remained the principal rival of the Vijayanagara Empire for nearly two centuries. Hence, the correct answer is Option (2).
Exam Note:
• Founder → Hasan Gangu (Ala-ud-Din Bahman Shah)
• Founded → 1347 CE

s: The bone of contention between the Bahmani Sultanate and Vijayanagar kingdom was
x: The Raichur Doab, between the Krishna and Tungabhadra rivers, was the main cause of Bahmani-Vijayanagara conflict.

s: Who among the following founded the Bahmani kingdom in the Deccan in the 14th century A.D.?
x: The Bahmani kingdom was founded in 1347 by Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah (Hasan Gangu), who revolted against Muhammad bin Tughlaq.

s: Who among the following shifted the Bahmani capital from Gulbarga to Bidar?
x: Ahmad Shah I (Ahmad Shah Wali) shifted the Bahmani capital from Gulbarga to Bidar around 1424.

s: Which one among the following was not a reform measure carried out by Mahmud Gawan of Bahmani Kingdom?
o: The Kingdom was divided into eight provinces or Tarafs.
Nobles were paid salaries and were asked to maintain contingents of horses.
A tract of land, Khalisa, was set apart for the expenses of the Tarafdar.
Lands were measured and land taxes were fixed on that basis.
x: Gawan's reform divided the 4 tarafs into 8 provinces and put forts under central commanders to curb nobles. The notes do not mention a Khalisa land tract set apart for the Tarafdar's expenses, so option 3 is the odd one out.

s:
Consider the following statements: The striking feature of the Jama Masjid in Kashmir completed by Zain-ul-Abidin include(s):
I. turret
II. similarity with Buddhist pagodas
III. Persian style
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
x: The Jama Masjid in Srinagar, extended by Zain-ul-Abidin, features turrets, pagoda-like roofs echoing Buddhist/Hindu traditions, and clear Persian architectural influence — all three elements together define its style.

s: Which among the following ruler abolished Jizya for first time?
x: Shahi Khan (Zain-ul-Abidin), the brother of Ali Shah, became the ruler of Kashmir in 1420 AD. He was the greatest king of Kashmir. He earned a name for his policy of religious tolerance and public welfare activities. He abolished Jizya tax on Hindus and banned cow slaughter. He was the first ruler to do so Mahabharata, Dashavatara and Rajtarangini were translated into the Persian language during his period. He was compared with Akbar due to his religious tolerance. The scriptures ‘Jain Prakash’ and Jain-Vilas’ were compiled during his rule. Also, he constructed artificial island of Zaina Lank in the middle of Wular Lake.

s: Ruler of Kashmir who was also known as “Akbar of Kashmir’ was-
x: Shahi Khan (Zain-ul-Abidin), the brother of Ali Shah, became the ruler of Kashmir in 1420 AD. He was the greatest king of Kashmir. He earned a name for his policy of religious tolerance and public welfare activities. He abolished Jizya tax on Hindus and banned cow slaughter. He was the first ruler to do so Mahabharata, Dashavatara and Rajtarangini were translated into the Persian language during his period. He was compared with Akbar due to his religious tolerance. The scriptures ‘Jain Prakash’ and Jain-Vilas’ were compiled during his rule. Also, he constructed artificial island of Zaina Lank in the middle of Wular Lake.

s: What was the original name of ruler of Kashmir Zainul-Abidin?
x: Zain-ul-Abidin's original name was Shahi Khan, brother of Ali Shah.

s: Which Sultan was reputed to be 'Akbar of Kashmir?
x: In 1420 A.D. brother of Ali Shah, Shahi Khan, sat on the throne of Kashmir with the name of Zain-ul-Abidin. He was greatest ruler of Kashmir who ruled for nearly 50 years. On account of his liberal religious policy, promotion of learning, and interest in art and architecture he was called 'Akbar of Kashmir'.

s: Which one of the following places was known as ‘Shiraz of East’ during the regime of Sharqi Rulers?
x: Jaunpur attained its greatest height under Sharqi Dynasty ruler, Ibrahim Shah (1402-1440 AD). He constructed some monuments in a new regional style of architecture known as the Sharqi architecture. Jaunpur was also known as the Shiraz of East or Shiraz-i-Hind during this period.

s: Who was the last ruler of 'Jaunpur' state?
x: Jaunpur city was founded in 14th century by Sultan Firuz Shah Tughluq and named in memory of his cousin, Muhammad- Bin Tughluq whose real name was Jauna Khan. In 1394 AD, Malik Sarwar established the independent Jaunpur state. Hussain Shah was the last ruler of Jaunpur state defeated by Bahlul Lodi. Jaunpur is historically known as 'Shiraz-i-Hind'. 6. Given below are two statements, in which one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R): Assertion (A): Jaunpur is known as Siraj-e-Hind. Reason (R): Jaunpur was a great centre of education during the Sharqi period. Select the correct answer using the code given below: Code - (a) (A) is false but (R) is true. (b) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is correct explanation of (A). (c) (A) is true but (R) is false. (d) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not correct explanation of (A). U.P. R.O./A.R.O. (Pre) 2023 Ans. (b) Ibrahim Shah Sharqi was the greatest ruler of the Sharqi dynasty of Jaunpur. He was a lover of knowledge and art. During his reign a new type of style, called 'Sharqi Art' emerged. In this style, the simple type of minarets was removed, and signs of Hindu influence started appearing in it. During his time, the cultural fame of Jaunpur spread all around and Jaunpur became famous by the name 'Siraj of India/East' or 'Shiraz-i-Hind'. Jaunpur emerged as a great center of education during the period of Sharqi rulers. Hence both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and R is correct explanation of A.

s: Which one of the following places was called “Shiraz of India”?
x: Jaunpur attained its greatest height under Sharqi Dynasty ruler, Ibrahim Shah (1402-1440 AD). He constructed some monuments in a new regional style of architecture known as the Sharqi architecture. Jaunpur was also known as the Shiraz of East or Shiraz-i-Hind during this period.

s: The capital of Sharqi dynasty during 15th-16th century AD was?

s: The main achievement of Bahlul Lodi was victory over which among the following regions?
